name: Tradie Ute
summary: The owner's dual-cab Mitsubishi Triton as a roster car (R123): tray, TJM-style bull bar, snorkel on the driver's A-pillar, roof rack, hi-vis tradie livery. Code-built from the Triton build script's proportions. Rear drive, 1900 kg: heavier and torquier than the Cruz, lower top speed.
feedback: Comment on this page (what to change, which view or state); the session turns each comment into a bug bead that cites this page and the car's id.

reference.note: Left to right per view: the Triton mesh's silhouette, the model's, and the diff (green is model outside the reference, red is reference the model misses). Both are bounding-box normalised. The Triton carries a canopy and a roof bag the model leaves out, and the model is a wider, caricatured stance, so the IoU is a recognisability check, not a fit target.

compare.label: LOD0 against the owner's Triton mesh (the reference is that mesh's own silhouettes, not photographs)

damage.note: Left to right: intact; door_FL and door_RL loose; front and back loose; wheel_FL cambered; front detached; door_FL detached; back (tray) detached; wheel_FL detached; both front doors and the tray detached; a stripped shell. Posed in a three.js viewer about each part's hinge line; the host renderer cannot draw a second vehicle yet.

paints.pattern: Seat colour on the paint key (white texels tint; the hi-vis livery, glass, lamps and tyres keep their colour), the number on the roof (anchor roof_number, between the rack rails) and in the HUD badge. docs/evidence/br-bwju.2/paints-strip.png shows white plus five player colours.

inWorld.label: Own car in its tile, large (1 tile, TV 1080p; viewer, not the host renderer)
From the Derby overview camera (top-down damage row)

findings.text: contract + reproducibility (validator clean, mass fractions sum 1.00, origin between the axles, anchors present, no badges or real names)

budget; silhouette: weighted IoU 0.757 against the owner's Triton mesh (side 0.757, top 0.798, front 0.716, rear 0.716). The model omits the canopy and the roof bag the Triton carries and is a wider, caricatured stance, so this is a recognisability check, not a fit target
paint key / one material (the Cruz's atlas layout and material; draw cost per tile is the Cruz's 11 parts)
damage states (each part rotates about its hinge line to its limit; detached parts lie as separate bodies; dark bays and interior blocks behind missing panels)
physics fit (convex colliders per part from the bake, profile geometry synced from the sidecar, settles with no NaN)
identity/readability at the smallest tile: legible in grid-24.png (roof stripes, tray, bull bar); the roof number is not drawn by this viewer, so number legibility is untested
engine sound: assets/audio/engine/tradie-ute.json derived from the Cruz profile (diesel-ish retune); `art/ui/poc/audio/engine/check.mjs` result is in the self-review

accel.note: engine force over mass at launch: an upper bound, drag and traction not included

topSpeed.note: Not measured yet: the R122 handling bank and the autopilot test assert envelopes. Three greybox laps under autopilot take 155 s against the Cruz's 151 s. R123's balance bead records the measured top speed.
